content:
The owner of the Bichon Frise named Weiwei, who was killed by a dog attack, posted a tribute on social media today, saying that Weiwei enjoyed going out and went for walks twice a day. Yesterday, while walking at a pet park, a dog nearly half the height of a person suddenly rushed out and bit Weiwei on the neck.

The owner recalled trying various methods, including kicking the large dog, spraying water at its nose, and using treats to distract it, but the dog held onto Weiwei tightly and refused to let go. The owner said: "I screamed for help and am grateful to the kind passers-by who assisted, but faced with a large dog weighing dozens of pounds that refused to release its grip, there was nothing anyone could do. I could only watch helplessly as my little dog lost her life."

Weiwei died on the spot. The owner recalled that the large dog remained guarding Weiwei's body until police arrived and brought it under control, after which the owner was finally able to collect the remains. "I later learned that the vicious dog had also killed another small dog. From beginning to end, the owner of the large dog never appeared."

The owner said the family was devastated by the sudden tragedy and unable to sleep all night. "Weiwei was an exceptionally well-behaved and gentle little dog, the little angel of our entire family. I so wish I could hold her again and kiss her. I cannot believe she has suddenly left us like this." The owner uploaded the last video of Weiwei before the incident, showing her sitting obediently and adorably in a stroller at a shopping mall. The owner said: "Only by repeatedly watching her curious and cute appearance can I temporarily forget the horrifying scene."

The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) replied to media inquiries yesterday, stating that after examination, the dog involved in the fatal attack had a microchip and a valid dog licence. The department will contact the owner based on the information on the licence and will investigate the incident, and will prosecute if there is sufficient evidence.

The AFCD pointed out that dog owners must keep their dogs under proper control at all times, including securely leashing large dogs, to avoid causing nuisance or harm to other people or animals. According to the Rabies Ordinance, dogs must be leashed or otherwise properly controlled when in public places, or in other locations where it can reasonably be expected that the dog may wander into a public place. Offenders may be fined HK$10,000.

集誌社 (Collective News) is currently querying the AFCD as to whether the dog owner has been contacted today, and is awaiting a reply.
